title: Bozoma Saint John Signs With CAA (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Bozoma Saint John has signed with CAA for representation.

	Saint John is a marketing executive and media personality best known serving in high-ran
body:
Bozoma Saint John has signed with CAA for representation.

	Saint John is a marketing executive and media personality best known serving in high-ranking roles at Apple, Uber, Endeavor and Netflix before going independent as well as joining “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” during Season 14.

	Saint John’s career began at Spike Lee’s creative agency SpikeDDB. She went on to become the head of music and entertainment marketing at PepsiCo before gaining significant attention for her work as head of global consumer marketing at Apple Music and iTunes. She then spent a year as Uber’s chief brand officer before serving as chief marketing officer at Endeavor and finally jumping to Netflix in the same role. Saint John worked at Netflix, where she was the first-ever Black C-suite executive, for two years from 2020 to 2022, and has been self-employed since then.
	

	In 2023, Saint John published via Penguin Random House a memoir titled “The Urgent Life,” which chronicled her grief and life as she lost her husband to cancer. In 2024, along with joining the cast of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills,” she launched the hair care brand Eve by Boz. The year after, she joined the NBC marketing competition series “On Brand With Jimmy Fallon” as co-host and mentor.


	Also among Saint John’s achievements are induction into the American Marketing Association Hall of Fame and the American Advertising Federation Hall of Achievement; being named one of Billboard’s Most Powerful Women in Music for 10 consecutive years and inducted into the publication’s Women in Music Hall of Fame; and being the subject of the Harvard Business School multimedia case study “Leading With Authenticity and Urgency.” Based on that case study, she developed and taught a class at Harvard titled “The Anatomy of a Badass” as well as a public online course titled “The Badass Workshop,” for which she went on an international tour across the U.S., Canada, Africa and Europe. Saint John also serves on the boards of Soho House and Vital Voices. 
	

	Along with CAA, Saint John continues to represented by Del Shaw Moonves Tanaka Finkelstein & Lezcano and Anita Chatterjee and Carrie Bernstein at A-Game Public Relations.

title: Kasie Hunt Takes Lead Role in CNN’s Fight to Keep Viewers From Toggling to Second Screen
description: Kasie Hunt is known best for her acumen in covering politics, but she is quickly developing an expertise in something that may even be more importan
body:
Kasie Hunt is known best for her acumen in covering politics, but she is quickly developing an expertise in something that may even be more important to her bosses at CNN: keeping TV-news viewers from jumping away to a second screen.

	On most afternoons, the  anchor leads conversations on “The Arena,” her late-day program that examines big stories in Washington. At many times, there is also a different kind of on-screen chatter. CNN has for months been experimenting with a “text chain” featuring lines of running commentary from reporters, experts and contributors who are not taking part in the discussions going on in Hunt’s studio. The effect? Viewers see a second conversation that looks a lot like what they might find on their smart phones.
	

	“I think it holds viewers,” says Hunt, during a recent interview. “You can hear from people who are professional journalists and experts, as opposed to the free-for-all” people often get when they turn to X, Threads or their own text conversations.


	CNN is trying to keep people who might gaze at a second screen focused instead on the first.

	Use of similar text-chain graphics has  spread to other types of programming. CNN featured a “live analysis” section on screen during its coverage of President Donald Trump’s remarks at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in late July. John Berman, Betsy Klein and Brian Stelter were among the personnel who could be seen offering comments as Trump spoke. CNN has used the design during certain live news events — a Capitol Hill hearing, or a Supreme Court oral argument, a court proceeding involving Trump when cameras were not allowed — when capturing the scene without interruption from anchors or correspondents is critical.
	

	There are thoughts about deploying the live chat elsewhere, says Abigail Crutchfield, CNN’s senior vice president of Washington and special events programming.  There could be value in a similar presentation during red carpet coverage at big awards events, or during a fashion showcase, she says during a recent interview. “We are offering our viewers and subscribers an opportunity to get what has sort of traditionally been seen when people are watching other screens, she says. Now, CNN sees a chance to “make it one screen and curate who are the experts.” Subscribers to CNN’s nascent “All Access” service can in some cases opt for a “feed” of text contributions that overlay linear shows.

	Can CNN out-tweet X and similar venues? All the mainstream news outlets ought to see if they can, argues Jaime Spencer, chief operating officer of Magid, a consultancy that advises TV stations and media companies. “There is certainly an engagement challenge with traditional platforms,” he says, noting the growing appeal of individual “creators” offering newsletters and video podcasts. “People are playing around with a lot of stuff, and they need to,” Spencer adds.

	Younger viewers — the ones who CNN and other outlets hope to cultivate in months and years to come — aren’t necessarily getting breaking news from traditional sources. Young adults are more likely to say they turn to search engines and social media for breaking news, according to a survey conducted in 2026 by Pew Research Center. Approximately,31% of adults under 30 indicated they turned to social media first to get more information about breaking events, while only 6% of Americans 65 and older said the same.

	Others have tried similar gambits. Fox News Channel’s Will Cain speaks into what appears to be a large radio microphone  — a signifier of the more freewheeling conversations held by video podcasters –during his daily afternoon hour on the network’s weekday schedule. MS NOW is expanding its use of taped video podcast segments from Crooked Media and other providers on weekend evenings. CNN has been spotted experimenting in real time, staging longtime host Anderson Cooper on screen in less formal environments and, on occasion, without a tie.

	And yet, some TV viewers may have seen such stuff before. Having short bits of text scroll across the screen evokes programs like “TRL,” the one-time music showcase from MTV that proved popular with younger viewers tuning in after school. The program often invited its audience to send in short messages, which producers would select and then scroll across the screen. The CNN technique may also remind audiences of “Pop-Up Video,” the VH-1 program that paired music videos, with little “bubbles” of information that would be appear alongside the entertainment.
	

	Hunt simply wanted to emulate something she has long used to help inform her reporting. “I run an email on big nights when I’m reporting on site,” she says. “I would just be in touch constantly with sources and then share the insights of that group.” Executives at CNN liked the idea, says Crutchfield, and thought it would get more information to viewers. “She has so many sources who could not be in studio every day,” she notes. “How do we bring that to the flow?”

	CNN has no hard data, but producers believe the “text chain” gets viewers to focus more closely on the linear screen, says Crutchfield, and perhaps delay any turn to a smartphone or social media platform for additional commentary. For viewers who may watch the show without audio, the comments give them more to watch. “It gives them another way to get deeper analysis than we could offer in a chyron or a banner,” she says.

	Use of the “text chain” creates new assignments behind the scenes. At “The Arena,” Hunt says, producers now book guests for the feature each day, usually from a group of reporters, correspondents and contributors that would take part in the traditional show at one time or another.

	“I’m a big believer that viewers really connect with people they see often,” says Hunt, who notes that text contributors often get different responses from viewers. “They get very specific feedback when they are on ‘text chain.’ People see what they are writing, and they will respond directly to an idea or thought, as opposed to when they sit in on set and hear, ‘Oh, I saw you on TV,” Hunt says. “I think a lot of people are surprised by the level of reaction they receive.”

	There are some limits. Viewers shouldn’t look for the freewheeling commentary and opinion that makes up so much of online chatter. “This is different from social media, or expressions in viewer comments, where you’re getting everyone’s opinion and is more unfiltered,” explains Crutchfield. “We are really focused on what matches our brand better, that expert context and analysis. We are trying to curate the room, and it’s really about the people who cover the subject, a lawyer, if that’s necessary or a White House reporter. It’s people who have knowledge.”
	

	A gatekeeper monitors the process in the studio but still must move quickly. A producer collects comments via the Slack short-form messaging platform, says Hunt, and examines comments to make sure they are not defamatory or outlandish. “In an era where we get an incredible volume of information with fewer tools to sort through whether that information is true and what is not,” CNN’s process helps it maintain its “trusted” status, Hunt says.

	There are no plans at present to deploy the on-screen “text chain” everywhere on CNN, says Crutchfield. The running text would distract from interviews of newsmakers, for example, but executives do see more chances to use it. When Hunt’s show televised an important Capitol Hill hearing for most of its hour, it relied on the host to offer analysis via the texts, so the event could be shown without interruption. At the start of the next hour, says Crutchfield, CNN abandoned the technique, thinking that it was specific to Hunt’s show. In the future, she suggests, producers might continue using it during live coverage.

	The on-screen commentary helps CNN vie more handily against a phalanx of digital competitors. “I think people are hungry” for more context, says Crutchfield. “That’s why so many people are going on social during events or speeches., Use of the new analysis tool “will evolve,” she says. “These are early days.”

title: ‘Harry Potter’ Series Star Bel Powley Says ‘I Strongly Disagree With J.K. Rowling’s Views on Gender’: ‘The Trans Community Deserve Safety and Dignity’
description: “Harry Potter” series star Bel Powley has spoken out about author J.K. Rowling‘s controversial views on gender, saying she “strongly disagrees” with
body:
“Harry Potter” series star Bel Powley has spoken out about author J.K. Rowling‘s controversial views on gender, saying she “strongly disagrees” with them. 

	Powley is playing Petunia Dursley in HBO‘s highly anticipated TV adaptation of the beloved books, the first season of which is set to premiere this Christmas. In the lead-up to the show, which Rowling is executive producing, members of the new cast — which also includes John Lithgow as Dumbledore, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape and Nick Frost as Hagrid — have faced questions over their participation due to Rowling’s beliefs, which have been criticized by many as anti-trans.
	

	In an interview with The Telegraph published on Monday, Powley said: “I strongly disagree with J.K. Rowling’s views on gender. I think that the trans community deserve safety and dignity and respect and total acceptance.”


	She then added, “But I love ‘Harry Potter.’ I grew up with the books. I am from that first generation of readers and, again, I love magic and spookiness.”

	Lithgow has also spoken about Rowling’s views several times, saying that he even considered walking away from the show but ultimately decided against it. “The reasons to do it were much, much stronger than the reasons to protest against what Rowling has done and said,” Lithgow told “The New Yorker Radio Hour” in April. “I do disagree with much of it, much of it I think has been twisted and misrepresented, and she has doubled down on it at her own cost.”

	The “Harry Potter” series cast also includes Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall and more. “Succession” helmer Mark Mylod directs, while Francesca Gardiner serves as showrunner. The series has already been renewed for a second season, which will adapt the second book, “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.”

title: Puerto Rico Needs More Than Thoughts and Prayers. Where Is Hollywood?
description:
Hey, Hollywood, Boricuas need you.

	On Friday, more than 180,000 households and businesses across San Juan and six neighboring municipalities woke
body:
Hey, Hollywood, Boricuas need you.

	On Friday, more than 180,000 households and businesses across San Juan and six neighboring municipalities woke up to dry faucets. For 48 hours at a stretch, on a rotating schedule with no end date, they will go without water. Roughly half a million people are being asked to live without the most basic need of a functioning society, and the silence around it is heartbreaking.


	The images coming out of the island should stop social media users in their tracks. Residents are filling buckets and jugs before their windows close. Elderly neighbors are depending on others to haul five-gallon jugs up apartment stairwells in punishing heat. Gov. Jennifer González calls the situation “out of our hands” and warns that the shutoffs could stretch to 72 hours if the rain does not come. July was the driest month San Juan has recorded in more than 120 years.
	

	This is not an “act of God,” but you already knew that.

	The island’s water authority loses well over half the water it treats before it ever reaches a tap, much of it bleeding out of pipes that have gone decades without adequate investment. Communities in and around the capital logged more than 100 days of outages this year before the rationing even began. The San Juan mayor sued the water authority in the spring. Residents have taken to the streets because they know that water is a right.

	A milder hurricane season is forecast, which sounds like mercy until you remember that the rain that refills the reservoirs often travels inside those storms. So, no, the cavalry is not coming from the weather.
	

	Which brings me to the burning question … where is Hollywood?

	I have spent my career watching the entertainment industry decide what deserves the world’s attention, and I have seen this community show up for Puerto Rico before. In 2017, days after Hurricane Maria left the island in the dark, Lin-Manuel Miranda wrote the benefit song “Almost Like Praying” and pulled in Jennifer Lopez, Marc Anthony, Gloria Estefan, Luis Fonsi, Rita Moreno, Rubén Blades, Camila Cabello and John Leguizamo, among others, naming all 78 of the island’s municipalities so none of them could be forgotten. It was a “We Are the World” of the moment. Every dollar went to the Hispanic Federation’s relief fund.

	Five years later, when Hurricane Fiona hit, Bad Bunny, Rauw Alejandro and others took relief into their own hands rather than wait for a slow federal response.

	Bad Bunny’s residency last year, “No Me Quiero Ir de Aquí,” reserved its first shows for locals, ran for more than 30 nights at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico and pumped an estimated $200 million into the economy during what is normally the island’s slow season.

	This proves that a star’s platform is not just a charity megaphone. It can be an economic engine. 

	The uncomfortable truth is that a water emergency is a hard story to sell in an attention-seeking economy. This tragic story can die without amplification. And amplification is the one thing Hollywood knows how to manufacture better than almost anyone.

	Puerto Rico needs its entertainment allies again, and it needs more than a repost.



	

					WILL TRENT — “He Lives!”
									Disney
	



	One who is not staying quiet is Ramón Rodríguez. The Puerto Rican star, executive producer and director of ABCs “Will Trent” brought the show to the island this past season, and he has used his platform to say plainly what too few in the industry will do.

	“People in Puerto Rico should not have to fight for the basic necessities of life,” Rodríguez tells Variety. “Water and electricity are not luxuries, they are essential. This is a humanitarian crisis, and it demands immediate action and lasting solutions.”

	Rodriguez also points to an organization, Plenitud PR, that could be supporting the efforts.

	“How can this be happening to this amazing community, and no FEMA or emergency help from this administration,” actor John Leguizamo asks bluntly. “These are citizens of the USA!”
	

	The island needs an event, a benefit, a telethon, anything that channels real money and real water to the people who need it. And should I remind everyone that Puerto Rico is part of the United States? Would another state be made to wait like this?

	Because we have seen the alternative before. After Hurricane Maria in 2017, a federal watchdog later found that billions in congressionally approved recovery funds were unnecessarily delayed by bureaucratic obstacles, and that officials obstructed the investigation into why. By one estimate, the holdup set the island’s recovery back years.

	This time around, the White House and Donald Trump have said … nothing. Even as hospitals, businesses and families brace for shortages that officials warn could last weeks or months, Puerto Rico has not been mentioned on any Truth Socials or tweets. But don’t worry, an incorrect use of an apostrophe (“America’s”) in Trump’s Truth Social post to talk about Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed was evidently a weekend requirement.

	The island’s resident commissioner has already put a five-point plan in front of the federal government and urged the governor to request an emergency declaration that would unlock FEMA support. Millions of American citizens are left to navigate a system that years of neglect had already hollowed out. The island also needs the Puerto Rican and Latino talent who have built billion-dollar franchises and sold out arenas to point their cameras at a leaking pipe and refuse to look away until Washington and the local government take action.

	The Emmys are quickly approaching, and Oscar season is a monthslong broadcast of some of the most-watched, most-quoted humans on earth standing at microphones. Every film festival is a chance to invoke Puerto Rico before a screening. Every one of those awards podiums is a chance to say the words “water” and “help” and “give” to an audience that might otherwise never hear about a reservoir running dry.

	None of this is a substitute for the government doing its job. The pipes are a public failure and they demand a public fix. But 3.2 million American citizens are living through a humanitarian crisis in real time, and the people with some of the loudest platforms in our culture have a documented, proven ability to force the rest of us to care.
	

	The people don’t need your thoughts and prayers. They need action.

	Do your part, please.

schema.headline: Puerto Rico Needs More Than Thoughts and Prayers. Where Is Hollywood?

title: Streaming Saves TV in Upfront, But Ad-Dollar Declines for Linear Are Significant
description:
The erosion of ad dollars earmarked for traditional TV has gone from alarming to dire.

	Advertisers cut their “upfront” spending on broadcast TV by
body:
The erosion of ad dollars earmarked for traditional TV has gone from alarming to dire.

	Advertisers cut their “upfront” spending on broadcast TV by approximately 5.3%, according to an analysis of the annual sales market by Media Dynamics Inc., a consultancy that tracks ad spending. Spending on cable TV fell even more, with marketers cutting outlays by 7.7%. In 2025, the spending decline for ad commitments for broadcast fell by just 2.5%, while ad commitments for cable were off by 4.3%. The estimates would mark the fourth consecutive year in which advertising money committed to broadcast and cable fell during the annual sales haggle.
	

	TV’s losses are growing as more advertisers rush to put money down where consumers are gravitating to most: sports and streaming. 


	The volume of ad commitments put toward streaming rose a whopping 30%, according to Media Dynamics, up to nearly $33.8 billion, compared with nearly $31 billion in 2025. Broadcast commitments in 2026, meanwhile, fell to $8.63 billion, compared with $9.1 billion last year. Cable commitments fell to nearly $8 billion in 2026, compared with nearly $8.7 billion in 2025.

	Thanks to streaming gains, the overall market rose 9.1%, Media Dynamics says, to about $33.8 billion, compared with nearly $31 billion last year. Advertisers again committed a greater amount of money to streaming than they did to either broadcast or cable primetime, for the third consecutive year.

	The numbers show just how dependent media companies both traditional and new-tech have become on video delivered via broadband connection. During the “upfront,” U.S. media companies try to sell the bulk of their commercial time tied to their next cycle of programming. Broadcast TV had long won the lion’s share of ad dollars, and, to be sure, some broadcast events, including NFL games and big special events, continue to win the biggest sums. But streaming is clearly connecting with Madison Avenue in away that undermines the sector’s traditional ways of making money.
	

	Most media companies so far have claimed victory in the upfront, but without offering too much detail. 

	Fox Corp. was able to nab a double-digit percentage increase in the volume of advertising tied to both Tubi and Fox News Channel, and “record” volume for sports and news, according to a person familiar with the matter. Amazon said it was able to sustain “year-over-year growth from new and existing advertisers,” but did not quantify whether any increases in volume were robust or less so. Paramount Skydance said last week it won “double-digit percentage” gains in upfront volume. Disney last week said the volume of ad commitments to its properties rose by a double-digit percentage over last year, with sports volume up in the “low teens.”

	Netflix on Monday said that it “nearly doubled our ad commitments this year, in line with expectations,” without specifying figures.

	While streaming will keep revenue flowing, the media companies appear to have lost some leverage in negotiations. 

	The cost of reaching 1,000 viewers, a key metric in these annual negotiations that is known as a CPM, is under clear pressure, according to Media Dynamics.

	CPMs fell across the board, at broadcast, cable and streaming. Broadcast CPMs fell 4.2%, to $41.65 from $43.50. Cable CPMS dropped 8.5%, to $17.70 from $19.35. Streaming CPMs fell 4.9%, to $25.90 from $27.75, according to Media Dynamics.  

	TV still has big bright spots. Disney said last week it had sold all of its advertising tied to its 2027 telecast of Super Bowl LXI, one of the earliest examples of sell-out of the Big Game occurring in recent memory.

schema.headline: Streaming Saves TV in Upfront, But Ad-Dollar Declines for Linear Are Significant

title: William H. Macy, Shawn Hatosy and Troy Kotsur Among Astra TV Awards Honorees; Lisa Ann Walter Set as Host
description: William H. Macy (“Train Dreams”), Shawn Hatosy (“The Pitt”) and Troy Kotsur (“CODA”) are among the actors set to be honored during this year’s Astra
body:
William H. Macy (“Train Dreams”), Shawn Hatosy (“The Pitt”) and Troy Kotsur (“CODA”) are among the actors set to be honored during this year’s Astra TV Awards ceremony, with Lisa Ann Walter (“Abbott Elementary”) hosting the show.

	Taking place Saturday at the InterContinental in Los Angeles, the Astra TV Awards celebrate performers making an impact with dedicated honorary awards. Macy will receive the timeless award, Hatosy will receive the virtuoso award and Kotsur will receive the impact award; additional honorees include Cedric the Entertainer (“Barbershop”) with the actor spotlight, Jason Ritter (“Matlock”) with the generations award and Natalie Alyn Lind (“Dutton Ranch”) with the TV breakout star award.
	

	“Lisa Ann Walter has built an extraordinary career by bringing humor, authenticity and heart to every role she takes on, making her the perfect host for this year’s celebration,” Astra Awards EVP Matt Weiss said in a statement. “We’re equally thrilled to honor all these remarkable artists, William H. Macy, Cedric the Entertainer, Shawn Hatosy, Natalie Alyn Lind, Jason Ritter, and Troy Kotsur, whose work continues to elevate television in unique and lasting ways.”


	Additionally, the list of confirmed presenters include Katherine LaNasa (“The Pitt”), William Stanford Davis (“Abbott Elementary”), Garret Dillahunt (“Lanterns”), Harry Goodwins (“The Gentlemen”), Sofia Rosinksy (“The Miniature Wife”), Katie Cassidy (“Accused: The Karen Read Story”), Taylor Polidore Williams (“Beauty in Black”) and Madeline Zima (“Subservience”), with more names to be announced.
	

	The ceremony will be livestreamed on The Astra Awards’ YouTube channel beginning at 7 p.m. PT on Saturday. Members of the Hollywood Creative Alliance, which include critics, entertainment journalists, content creators, industry insiders and creatives, vote on the awards.

schema.headline: William H. Macy, Shawn Hatosy and Troy Kotsur Among Astra TV Awards Honorees; Lisa Ann Walter Set as Host

title: Rohit Sharma, Ajay Devgn, Madhuri Dixit Nene and A.R. Rahman Lead Sony Pictures Networks India Content Slate
description: Star Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma is stepping into entertainment for the first time, fronting a new show set to launch in September on Sony Enterta
body:
Star Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma is stepping into entertainment for the first time, fronting a new show set to launch in September on Sony Entertainment Television and streamer SonyLIV, as Sony Pictures Networks India unveiled an expansive content slate spanning fiction, reality, sports and regional programming.

	“We have announced a show with active India cricket star Rohit Sharma. And Rohit will start anchoring and presenting his own show on SET and SonyLIV in September,” said Gaurav Banerjee, managing director and CEO of Sony Pictures Networks India.
	

	The slate’s marquee title is “Kaun Banega Crorepati” Season 18,” which premiered on Sony Entertainment Television and Sony LIV under the new campaign line “Sochna Padega.” As revealed by Variety, the new season, hosted by Indian cinema legend Amitabh Bachchan, is the franchise’s first to be crafted with artificial intelligence, shifting the show’s focus from trivia recall toward reasoning under pressure.


	Top Bollywood star Ajay Devgn will host true-crime series “Crime Patrol 2026,” bringing real-life cases to viewers through the franchise’s established storytelling format. Bharti Singh and Harsh Limbachiyaa will host comedy format “Indian Game Show,” bringing celebrities together for a series of challenges.

	Bollywood icon Madhuri Dixit Nene will front “Kon Honar Crorepati,” the Marathi-language edition of the “Kaun Banega Crorepati” format, which is the Indian adaptation of “Who Wants to be a Millionaire?” Banerjee said Dixit Nene “has broken the glass ceiling more than once, and we are really confident that she can and she will be able to do this again.”
	

	Oscar-winning composer A.R. Rahman will lead “Tamil Idol,” the first Tamil-language version of the singing competition format, searching for Tamil Nadu’s next major vocal talent. SonyLIV will also stream “MasterChef Tamil,” featuring star Samantha Ruth Prabhu.

	Also joining the lineup is “Scam 2010,” a production from Birla Studios, Applause Entertainment and SonyLIV, helmed by Indian National Film Award winning director Hansal Mehta and starring Pratik Gandhi, which has begun shooting. The show had drawn a legal challenge from Sahara India Pariwar following its announcement in May 2025. Asked by Variety whether the dispute had been resolved, Banerjee said, “I believe so.” Sony LIV will additionally carry the digital and television premiere of “Haiwaan,” Priyadarshan’s upcoming film starring Akshay Kumar and Saif Ali Khan, following its theatrical release.

	Sony Sports Network will complement the entertainment offering with its Festival of Sports, an Aug. 15-Dec. 1 window covering India’s cricket tour of Sri Lanka, the Women’s T20 Asia Cup cricket, the Asian Games and India’s all-format cricket tour of New Zealand.

	SPNI, which Sony Group Corporation owns indirectly and in full, runs 29 premium channels spanning Hindi, Marathi, Bangla and English general entertainment, movies, kids and factual programming, alongside Sony Sports Network and streaming platform SonyLIV, reaching more than 700 million viewers across India with distribution in over 150 countries.

schema.headline: Rohit Sharma, Ajay Devgn, Madhuri Dixit Nene and A.R. Rahman Lead Sony Pictures Networks India Content Slate

title: Awards Season Shuffles to 2027: From Denzel Washington’s ‘Here Comes the Flood’ to Joel Coen’s ‘Jack of Spades,’ Plus A24’s Mystery Drop (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Don’t believe every Oscar list you read.

	With the fall festivals gearing up for launch and studios locking in their year-end release plans, a hand
body:
Don’t believe every Oscar list you read.

	With the fall festivals gearing up for launch and studios locking in their year-end release plans, a handful of high-profile titles that many had penciled into the 2026 awards conversation are not likely to drop this year. Some are moving to 2027, others are still searching for a distributor and a few need more time in the edit bay.

	None of this is a referendum on the work, and it should not be read as such. In an awards ecosystem that increasingly rewards a clean runway and a well-timed festival launch, holding a film can be the savvier play, and a packed slate can force even a strong contender to wait its turn. Here is a look at the titles poised to sit out this year’s race, several of which Variety has confirmed exclusively, and the thinking behind each.
	



	

					Charles Melton at the Gold House 5th Annual Gold Gala held at The Music Center on May 09, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
									Gilbert Flores/Variety
	



	“Saturn Return” (Netflix)


	Greg Kwedar’s follow-up to the Oscar-nominated “Sing Sing” is a Chicago-set romance that unfolds across two timelines, tracing a decade in the lives of three college friends. Charles Melton, a 2026 Emmy nominee for the Netflix anthology series “Beef,” stars alongside Emmy winner Rachel Brosnahan and the always remarkable Will Poulter, with Plan B producing. Once expected to bow this year, the drama could instead set its sights on a March launch at South by Southwest (SXSW) in Austin, the same festival that introduced “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” That would fold it into the next awards conversation rather than this one.
	



	

					Director Fernando Meirelles‘The Two Popes’ film presentation, The Contenders London presented by Deadline Hollywood, Ham Yard Hotel, London, UK – 05 Oct 2019
									Vianney La Caer/Deadline Hollywood/Shutterstock
	



	“Here Comes the Flood” (Netflix)

	Fernando Meirelles, the Oscar-nominated director of “City of God” who also helmed “The Two Popes,” steers this unconventional heist thriller from a Simon Kinberg script, described as the story of a bank guard, a teller and a master thief caught in a deadly game of cons and double-crosses, told in a nonlinear fashion. Denzel Washington leads a cast that includes Robert Pattinson (this would have been his fifth film of the calendar year, alongside “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” “Primetime” and “Dune: Part Three”), Daisy Edgar-Jones (who also stars in the upcoming “Sense and Sensibility” remake), Danai Gurira and Sean Harris. The production shot in New Jersey into late January, leaving a tight post-production window, and with Netflix’s year-end film slate already stacked, the smart money has “Flood” debuting in 2027.

	Netflix’s slate is already fairly stacked, anchored by Cannes acquisitions “La Bola Negra,” which shared the festival’s best director prize, and “Gentle Monster,” starring French star Léa Seydoux. And still to come from the streaming giant are the untitled sequel to “Once Upon a Time in…Hollywood” from director David Fincher, scheduled to be released in IMAX on Nov. 25, the war drama “The Mosquito Bowl” from Peter Berg, and the Venice Film Festival opener “Ink” from Danny Boyle.



	

									Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images
	



	“The Riders” (A24)

	Edward Berger, coming off “Conclave” and “All Quiet on the Western Front,” teams with Brad Pitt for a psychological thriller adapted by David Kajganich from Tim Winton’s 1994 novel. This would have been a third 2026 title for Pitt, who also has the “Once Upon a Time in…Hollywood” sequel from Fincher and David Ayer’s “Heart of the Beast” on the docket.

	Emmy winner Julianne Nicholson, Danny Huston and Camille Cottin round out the ensemble. Production only got underway across Europe in early 2026, which makes a finish this year a stretch and points the film toward 2027.



	

					Ruben Östlund
									Dan Doperalski for Variety
	



	“The Entertainment System Is Down” (A24)

	Two-time Palme d’Or winner Ruben Östlund’s English-language satire strands an ensemble on a long-haul flight between London and Sydney, where the failure of the in-flight entertainment system forces passengers to confront the horror of boredom. Keanu Reeves, Oscar nominee Kirsten Dunst, Daniel Brühl, Nicholas Braun and two-time Oscar nominee Samantha Morton headline a sprawling cast shot around a real Boeing 747 the director acquired for the production. Östlund reportedly pulled the film from the 2026 Cannes lineup and has said he does not expect to finish before year’s end, with a Cannes premiere now eyed for 2027.
	

	A24, by contrast, is adding rather than subtracting. Even with two of its titles above sliding out of 2026, the distributor is running a deep bench this year, starting with the already-released summer comedy hit “The Invite” from Olivia Wilde. Still to come: Jesse Eisenberg’s original musical “The Debut,” Chris Rock’s Hollywood drama “Misty Green,” Lance Oppenheim’s “To Catch a Predator”-inspired “Primetime” and Jordan Firstman’s “Club Kid,” which the company acquired at Cannes. 

	According to sources, A24 is also expected to slot one more film into its 2026 roster. Among the undated candidates, Jody Hill’s “Famous,” with Zac Efron, Phoebe Dynevor and Nicholas Braun, reads as one of the likeliest additions. Henry Dunham’s crime thriller “Enemies,” with Jeremy Allen White and Austin Butler, is not expected to be the one, with that title more likely to surface in 2027.

	We could also speculate whether any of its 2027 films would be one that could make early appearances, such as Sean Durkin’s “Deep Cuts,” an adaptation of the novel by Holly Brickley, which stars Cailee Spaeny and Drew Starkey, with Josh Safdie, Ronald Bronstein and Eli Bush among the producing team.



	

					NEW YORK, NEW YORK – MAY 06: Josh O’Connor attends The 2024 Met Gala Celebrating “Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion” at The Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 06, 2024 in New York City. (Photo by Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)
									Getty Images
	



	Still looking for homes

	Two prestige packages still without a home are also unlikely to surface this year.

	Tom Ford’s “Cry to Heaven,” the designer-turned-filmmaker’s first feature since 2016’s “Nocturnal Animals,” adapts Anne Rice’s 1982 novel set in the ruthless world of 18th-century Italian opera. Ford writes, directs and produces, with a cast that includes Nicholas Hoult, Colin Firth, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Grammy winner Adele in her acting debut. Filming began in January in London and Rome, and with no distributor yet attached, the film is expected to land a buyer and arrive in the next calendar year.

	Academy Award winner Joel Coen’s “Jack of Spades,” meanwhile, wrapped in Glasgow late last year and has screened for several prospective studios. The gothic mystery, set in 1880s Scotland, marks Coen’s second solo directorial outing after “The Tragedy of Macbeth” and stars Josh O’Connor, Frances McDormand, Lesley Manville and Damian Lewis, with regular collaborators Bruno Delbonnel behind the camera and Carter Burwell on the score. Sources tell Variety that the initial cut ran nearly 150 minutes but showed immense promise, and a tighter second version has screened in recent weeks, and appears to have hit the sweet spot. An acquisition announcement is expected sooner rather than later.
	



	

					OAK BLUFFS, MASSACHUSETTS – AUGUST 07: (L-R) Thuso Mbedu, Gina Prince-Bythewood and Sunny Hostin attend the “Children of Blood and Bone” Exclusive Footage and Conversation during the Martha’s Vineyard African American Film Festival on August 07, 2026, in Oak Bluffs, Massachusetts. (Photo by Arnold Turner/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures)
									Arnold Turner/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures
	



	Listed for 2027, and they mean it

	Already known, but worth mentioning again: Neon’s “A Place in Hell,” director Chloe Domont’s follow-up to her Sundance sensation “Fair Play,” was once positioned for a Christmas Day release, but Neon has since moved the adult thriller to April 23, 2027. The film stars Michelle Williams as a cutthroat criminal defense attorney on the verge of making partner whose ambitions are upended when a younger lawyer, played by Daisy Edgar-Jones, is brought in to replace her, with the rivalry escalating to dangerous extremes. Andrew Scott also stars, who has the highly anticipated “Elsinore” coming later this year.

	Paramount Pictures’ “Children of Blood and Bone,” Gina Prince-Bythewood’s long-gestating adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi’s bestselling “Legacy of Orïsha” fantasy, locked for Jan. 15, 2027, a prime Martin Luther King Jr. weekend slot, and the date immediately raised the prospect of whether Paramount would mount a late-2026 qualifying run. Sources at the studio say it will not: the ensemble epic is being positioned to launch fresh at the start of a new calendar year rather than chase this season. The starry cast includes Thuso Mbedu, Damson Idris, Amandla Stenberg, Cynthia Erivo, Lashana Lynch, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Regina King, Idris Elba and Viola Davis. The decision is not a surprise given the off-screen turbulence that has trailed the production, with Adeyemi, who co-wrote the screenplay, publicly distancing herself from the film and saying she had blocked its star, Stenberg, on social media, according to the L.A. Times.

	For awards handicappers, the takeaway is that slates get crowded, edits run long and a strategic hold can be worth more than a rushed cut just to “be in the conversation.”

schema.headline: Awards Season Shuffles to 2027: From Denzel Washington’s ‘Here Comes the Flood’ to Joel Coen’s ‘Jack of Spades,’ Plus A24’s Mystery Drop (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Peacock Launches AI-Generated ‘Public Eye’ Mobile Detective Game From Wolf Games
description: NBCUniversal’s Peacock app has launched AI-generated title “Public Eye,” a serialized detective mobile game from the Dick Wolf-backed Wolf Games.
body:
NBCUniversal’s Peacock app has launched AI-generated title “Public Eye,” a serialized detective mobile game from the Dick Wolf-backed Wolf Games.

	Per the description for the game, players take on the role of Officer Logan Dine, “a patrol cop secretly investigating his uncle’s murder in the crime-ridden streets of Caldera City. Every episode features narrative storytelling with puzzle-driven gameplay, inviting players to search animated scenes for clues, ultimately revealing a conspiracy that runs through the entire police department. The AI-generated visuals paired with Wolf Games’ storytelling expertise create a seamless experience that allows users to drive the story forward themselves.”
	

	The title was first announced last October, when Wolf Games (founded by Andrew Adashek, Noah Rosenberg and Dick Wolf’s son, Elliot Wolf) launched a partnership with NBCUniversal.


	Wolf Games’ “Public Eye” is the latest game to join the Peacock app, which currently includes “Law & Order: Clue Hunter” (also from Wolf Games), “Jeopardy! TODAY” and “Wheel of Fortune TODAY.” According to Peacock, 40% of Peacock mobile users engaged with a game on the app in June and early insights show “Law & Order: Clue Hunter” players are averaging more than six minutes a day in the game.

	“’Public Eye’ sits right at the intersection of two trends users are excited about: microdramas and interactive storytelling,” NBCUniversal Media Group senior vice president of product UX and design John Jelley said. “This new experience invites fans to step into the story rather than simply watch it unfold. Through our work with Wolf Games, we’re exploring how Peacock can bring together video, gameplay, and storytelling in a single destination, creating more opportunities for audiences to engage with the worlds they love throughout the day.”
	

	“’Public Eye’ was built to be incredibly easy to step into,” Wolf Games co-founder Elliot Wolf said. “Within seconds you’re spotting clues, meeting characters and feeling a high-stakes story come together under your fingers. It’s a new world of crime and betrayal that keeps you on the edge of your seat and coming back episode after episode. Immersive and cinematic, but as easy to pick up as your morning puzzle.”

schema.headline: Peacock Launches AI-Generated ‘Public Eye’ Mobile Detective Game From Wolf Games

title: Samuel Goldwyn Acquires North America Rights to WestEnd Films’ Holiday Comedy ‘Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: WestEnd Films has negotiated a North American deal with Samuel Goldwyn Films on behalf of the filmmakers for the feel-good Christmas comedy “Merry C
body:
WestEnd Films has negotiated a North American deal with Samuel Goldwyn Films on behalf of the filmmakers for the feel-good Christmas comedy “Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint,” which will be released theatrically in the U.S. and Canada this Christmas.

	The deal follows Signature Entertainment’s acquisition of U.K. and Ireland rights during Cannes earlier this year, with a theatrical release also planned for this holiday season.


	In addition to North America and the U.K., WestEnd has also sold the film to Spain (Alfa), Portugal (Nos), Bulgaria (Beta) and Israel (United King), and it will continue international sales at Toronto Film Festival.
	

	Directed by Jack Spring (“All Town Aren’t We,” “Three Day Millionaire”) and written by Chris Boyle-McQuarry (“Little Lady”), the film’s ensemble cast includes John Bradley (“Game of Thrones,” “Marry Me,” “Moonfall”), Celia Imrie (“The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel,” “Calendar Girls”), Richard E. Grant (“Argylle,” “Saltburn,” “Can You Ever Forgive Me?”), Adjoa Andoh (“Bridgerton,” “The Witcher”) and Jim Broadbent (“Paddington,” “The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry,” “Moulin Rouge”).

	The cast also includes Sophia Di Martino, Adrian Rawlins, Karl Pilkington, Kiell Smith-Bynoe, Nigel Planer, Ann Mitchell, Dave Johns, Dustin Demri-Burns, Harriet Webb and rising young actor Beau Thompson.

	With a Dickensian twist, “Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint” follows Aubrey Flint, a reclusive model soldier painter who despises Christmas. Sentenced to community service at a struggling retirement home, Aubrey is reluctantly drawn into directing a chaotic resident-led production of “A Christmas Carol.” As rehearsals descend into comic mayhem, and with the future of Willow Lodge at risk, Aubrey is forced to confront his own grief and rediscover the unexpected magic of friendship, community and Christmas cheer.
	

	The film is produced by Andy Brunskill (“Sweet Sue,” “Lilting,” “Everything Now”) for SUMS Film & Media alongside Spring’s Shush Films and in association with BYUtv. Damian Jones (“The Iron Lady,” “Goodbye Christopher Robin,” “Rye Lane,” “Belle”) and Paul Grindey (“The Father,” “Bad Apples,” “Rye Lane”) of Viewfinder serve as executive producers, along with Shush’s Andrew Pettit, BYUtv’s Andra Johnson Duke and Wendy Thomas, CPR Entertainment’s Craig Hemmings and Rick Guard, individual EP’s Miles Gooseman, Jessica Gooseman, Steven J. Toll and Randy Jones Toll, Simon Herring and the Warner Group Media’s Mark Warner, Lise Abraham, Simon White and Ian McCulloch.

	The deal was negotiated by Maya Amsellem, managing director at WestEnd Films, on behalf of the filmmakers, and Miles Fineburg at Samuel Goldwyn Films.

	“We’re thrilled to be bringing ‘Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint’ to audiences this fall. This is the kind of classic heartfelt story that families love for the holiday season – funny, warm and full of surprises right up to the final frame,” said Miles Fineburg, vice president of acquisitions and sales at Samuel Goldwyn Films.

	Amsellem said: “ ‘Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint’ has all the ingredients of an enduring festive favorite: a brilliant ensemble cast, genuine warmth, sharp comedy and a moving story about friendship and community. We are delighted to be working once again with Samuel Goldwyn, a long-standing and trusted partner, to bring the film to North American audiences this Christmas.”

schema.headline: Samuel Goldwyn Acquires North America Rights to WestEnd Films’ Holiday Comedy ‘Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: 'A Christmas Story' Actress Tedde Moore Dead at 79
description:
'A Christmas Story' Tedde Moore
                          Dead At 79
body:
'A Christmas Story' Tedde Moore
                          Dead At 79
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            4:04 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 10, 2026
                                5:24 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Actress Tedde Moore -- who famously played Miss Shields in "A Christmas Story" — has died.
      
    
            Moore passed away last Wednesday in Huntsville, Ontario, Canada, according to a Facebook post under her name. Her cause of death was not released.
      
    
            Moore kicked off her acting career by starring alongside Christopher Walken in the play, "A Midsummer Night's Dream," in Stratford, Ontario. 
      

            She then landed her biggest role as Miss Shields in the hit 1983 film, "A Christmas Story." Moore was unforgettable as the uber-strict teacher of 9-year-old Ralphie Parker, played by Peter Billingsley.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Moore also secured roles in other films, such as "Second Wind," "Murder by Decree," "Overnight," and "Down the Road Again."
      
    
            Her credits on the small screen included the TV movie, "Mistletoe over Manhattan," and the mini-series, "The Kennedys."
      
    
            Moore was 79.
      
    
            RIP

                            8:40 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A gaudy Palm Springs pool party went from bottles popping to bottles flying ... leaving nine people injured and seven rushed to the emergency room after The Chainsmokers played a set.
      
    
            The chaos erupted early Sunday during Splash House's "After Hours" event at the Palm Springs Air Museum.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Palm Springs Police say officers working the festival were alerted to an assault around 1:37 AM ... after a dispute broke out and escalated into bottles being hurled into the crowd.
      
    
            Police say nine partygoers who had nothing to do with the original altercation were injured ... with some getting cut by broken glass.
      

        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Cops say seven people were taken to a local hospital, while two others were treated at the scene. All of the injuries were described as minor.
      
    
            The Chainsmokers headlined the overnight event, with Ship Wrek also on the bill.
      
    
            PSP is investigating and has not publicly identified any suspects.

title: Insane Videos Show Colombia's 7.4 Magnitude Earthquake, At Least 22 Dead
description:
Colombia Earthquake
                          Insane Videos Show 7.4 Magnitude Jolt
body:
Colombia Earthquake
                          Insane Videos Show 7.4 Magnitude Jolt
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            9:18 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
            A massive 7.4 magnitude earthquake rocked western Colombia on Monday ... killing at least 22 people, collapsing buildings and leaving others trapped beneath the rubble ... and video shows the heartbreaking aftermath.
      
    
            The quake struck near San José del Palmar in the Chocó region, with powerful shaking felt across the country, CNN reports.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Footage from several cities shows clouds of dust filling the streets as building facades crumble and residents race for cover.
      
    
            Reuters reports 18 people were killed in Pereira, while 3 others died in Manizales, and 1 death was reported in the region of Antioquia. Rescue crews are searching damaged buildings for more victims.
      

            In Cali, officials say around 25 structures collapsed ... trapping people inside and forcing the city to call in additional rescue teams. Injuries and serious damage were also reported in Quibdó, the capital of Chocó.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The tremors sent alarms blaring in Bogotá and forced people out of buildings, though officials there initially reported only cracks and no serious structural damage.
      
    
            Flights were suspended at several airports while crews inspected the facilities.
      
    
            Officials are warning residents about possible aftershocks, but authorities say there is no tsunami threat.

            Kim Kardashian had some real drama over the weekend ... a suspect allegedly burglarized the reality star's L.A. mansion and took her staffer's car for a joyride before getting arrested.
      
    
            Law enforcement sources tell TMZ ... the 27-year-old man showed up Sunday afternoon at Kim's Hidden Hills estate, which is under renovation, and forced his way inside through a door. 
      
    
            We're told Kim and her kids are NOT living on the property while the home is under renovation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Our sources say the man took items from Kim's house and loaded them into a vehicle. 
      
    
            We're told the man also got behind the wheel of a car belonging to a Kim staffer and took it for a spin around the neighborhood.
      

            Our sources say a security guard saw the car driving around and followed it back to Kim's home before calling the sheriff's office. We're told sheriff deputies surrounded Kim's home and eventually took the man into custody without further incident.
      
    
            Police say nobody was injured and no weapons were found on the suspect, who was arrested on suspicion of burglary.
      
    
            Sources close to Kim say she and her kids have been living in a rental for the past few months.
      
    
            Our Kim sources also disputed parts of the police narrative, saying the suspect never gained entry to the home and Kim does not have any of her stuff there right now.
